plugin.name: OpenBao Secrets
plugin.description: Keep secrets in OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault, type them at a terminal's password prompt, and let other plugins store theirs.

use.title: Use secrets
use.description: Keep your own secrets, read the shared ones, type them into terminals, and run other plugins' actions that use this plugin.

manageShared.title: Manage shared secrets
manageShared.description: Add, replace and delete the shared secrets.

createAppSecrets.title: Create app secrets
createAppSecrets.description: Let plugins add a new secret field, for you, at the app paths an admin allows. It never reads or replaces one.

address.label: OpenBao address
address.description: The https address of OpenBao or Vault, with the port. http is refused.

caPem.label: CA certificate (PEM)
caPem.description: Trust only this CA for OpenBao. Leave it empty to use the server's normal trust store, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS included.

kvMount.label: KV mount
kvMount.description: The KV version 2 secrets engine to use.

basePath.label: Base path
basePath.description: The folder in the KV mount that holds everything this plugin writes.

roleId.label: AppRole role ID
roleId.description: The role ID of the AppRole the plugin logs in with. It is not secret. The secret ID comes through Connect below.

appsBasePath.label: App secrets folder
appsBasePath.description: A folder in the KV mount where other programs read their secrets, as <folder>/<app>/<host>. Empty: plugins cannot create app secrets. It must be outside the base path.

allowedAppPaths.label: Allowed app paths
allowedAppPaths.description: One <app>/<host> per line, under the app secrets folder. Plugins may add a field there that does not exist yet; they never read or replace one. Empty: off.

status.notConnected: OpenBao Secrets is not connected. Ask an admin to connect OpenBao Secrets.
status.adminHint: Connect it in Settings, Plugins, OpenBao Secrets.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Up to 4 parts joined by /. Each part is letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'.
form.nameRule: Use up to 4 parts of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', joined by /
form.valueHint: Check the value before you save it: once saved, it is never shown again.
form.noteHint: A short note, not secret, shown in the list.
form.noteRule: A note is at most {{max}} characters

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.description: Every version of this secret is deleted from OpenBao. This cannot be undone.

picker.title: Type a secret
picker.caution: The secret is typed at the cursor. Use it at a password prompt: at a normal prompt it shows on screen and in history.
picker.empty: There are no secrets to type.
picker.noTerminal: No open terminal took the secret
picker.variableCaution: Use this only at a bash or zsh prompt, not inside another program: it types a command. The value goes into the variable without showing on screen or going into history.
picker.variableHint: Letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit.
picker.variableRule: Use letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit, at most {{max}} characters
picker.variableShell: The shell uses {{variable}} itself: pick another name
picker.variableUnfit: This secret has more than one line or a control character, or is too long, so it cannot go in a variable: type it at the cursor
picker.put: Put {{name}} in ${{variable}}. Use "${{variable}}" in commands, and run unset {{variable}} when done.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Connect with a response-wrapped AppRole secret ID. The secret ID is kept sealed on the server and never shown.
connection.notRunning: Turn the plugin on to connect it.
connection.tokenHint: Make one with: vault write -wrap-ttl=10m -f auth/approle/role/<role>/secret-id (or bao write). It works once.
connection.disconnectDescription: The stored secret ID is deleted. Nobody can read or type secrets until an admin connects again. The secrets stay in OpenBao.
connection.loginFailed: Connected, but the first login failed
